meta.description: Engineering knowledge graph for the autonomous loop: typed nodes + directed edges. Evidence-only-append. Decisions never deleted (supersede only).

nodes.summary: TokenService mutations run through a transaction-scoped repository (Repository.WithTx); multi-step writes share one SQLite tx and roll back together instead of hand-rolled compensation.
nodes.rationale: TransferFrom previously attempted best-effort allowance/balance compensation on mid-transaction failure, which had multiple failure modes (compensation itself failing). Real transactions give atomicity for free.

nodes.summary: State that can be concurrently incremented/decremented (token balances/supply/allowances, voting tallies, NFT ownership) MUST be changed via atomic conditional-UPDATE repository primitives (TryAddBalance, TrySubtractFromSupply, TryDeductApproval, IncrementCandidateVoteCount, TryTransferOwnership), never read-modify-write in the service/use-case layer.
nodes.rationale: read-modify-write loses updates under concurrency (proven lost-update bugs: token Mint Round 32, voting tally this round). SQLite per-connection write serialization makes conditional UPDATE atomic.

nodes.summary: Burn decremented only the owner's balance, not total_supply, breaking the ledger invariant total_supply == sum(balances).
CastVoteUseCase incremented candidate.VoteCount via read-modify-write; two concurrent voters to the same candidate lost one increment.
ErrAmountTooLarge (>MaxInt64) was missing from the handler error-classification map, so over-supply requests returned 500 instead of 400.

eventBus.Publish writes events.db (a separate DB file from tokens.db) while INSIDE the token tx callback (ordered first, before balance/supply mutations). On any later in-tx failure the tx rolls back but the event stays, so history shows operations that never applied (phantom audit events).
nodes.evidence: internal/app/wire.go creates separate events.db/tokens.db/nonces.db; service.go Publish is the first statement inside WithTransaction for Mint/Transfer/TransferFrom/Burn

nodes.summary: SQLite primitives CAST(total_supply/balance AS INTEGER); once an accumulated supply/balance exceeds MaxInt64 the CAST saturates and further mints/transfers change nothing — silent loss. Individual amounts are capped by ValidateAmount but accumulation is not.

NFT (SaveNFT + SaveOperation + chain.AddBlock) and voting (TryMarkVoted + SaveVote + tally) use best-effort compensation instead of real transactions; compensation errors are silently swallowed (_ = repo.DeleteNFT). Accepted debt, documented in-service.
fix(token): transaction-scoped repo writes + Burn total_supply decrement (TrySubtractFromSupply), NewTokenFromRecord faithful reconstruction, ValidateAmount >MaxInt64 guard. Commit caa2c94.
fix(api): classify ErrAmountTooLarge as 400/AMOUNT_TOO_LARGE; removed dead TxExecutor/TxRepository. Commit 7e4f193.
fix(voting): atomic IncrementCandidateVoteCount closes lost-update race. Commit 591d8d9.
Oracle fetcher followed redirects into loopback/private/link-local IPs and non-HTTP schemes (SSRF via redirect; cloud-metadata primitives reachable if a source URL is compromised).
fix(http): CheckRedirect blocks SSRF redirects to internal/private destinations + non-HTTP schemes. Commit 30b3748.
Initial SSRF guard matched IP literals only; hostname redirects (localhost, metadata.google.internal, DNS names in RFC1918 space) bypassed it. Found by adversarial code review.
TestTransferFrom_AtomicityOnAllowanceDeductionFailure overclaimed: injected failure fired on the first mutation, so no partial state existed; name said 'Atomicity' but verified nothing rolled back.
fix(http): DNS-resolve hostname redirects for SSRF blocking; pinned flaky concurrent test; renamed + added genuine mid-tx rollback atomicity tests. Commit 55554a8.
test(infra): migrate coverage 74.1%->81.5% (error branches); backup error-path tests. Commit e8c27dc.
fix(token): reject supply/balance increments past MaxInt64 (conditional bounds on TryAddToSupply and TryAddBalance DO UPDATE). Commit fcd05d8.
fix(token): clamp allowance increases at MaxInt64 in TryAdjustApproval (MIN-with-CAST ceiling). Commit a12cd62.
RegisterVoter/RegisterCandidate/CreateSession accepted empty names, empty or unknown candidate sets, and sessions whose end time preceded start — no boundary validation.
fix(voting): fail-fast validation + sentinel errors for voter/candidate/session input; 400 classification. Commit 8cf8ced.

BlockChain.AddBlock appends in-memory only; the blocks table is loaded at init but nothing persists new blocks, so the chain resets to genesis and re-stamps heights on every restart. BlockchainRepository (SaveBlock/GetAllBlocks) is built but never wired — orphaned persistence layer.
nodes.evidence: init.go loads+inserts genesis only; service.go/nft service.go AddBlock call sites never write to DB; sqlite/blockchain.go BlockchainRepository unreferenced in production

nodes.summary: TryAdjustApproval increase past MaxInt64 stored an unparseable REAL float, corrupting the allowance for TransferFrom. Same class as supply/balance saturation.
Cross-DB non-atomicity: audit event written inside the token tx callback survives a rollback (phantom history entries); chain.AddBlock and replay nonces likewise outside the tx.
Cumulative supply/balance can exceed MaxInt64 (per-op guard passes) and later CAST(...) clamps silently; detect/reject post-arithmetic overflow.

NFT (SaveNFT/SaveOperation) and voting (TryMarkVoted/SaveVote/tally) use best-effort compensation instead of real transactions; crash leaves partial state. Accepted debt; convert when touchpoint opens.
backup package at 73.8%: remaining uncovered lines are Close/Copy I/O error branches not worth contriving; migrate now 81.5%.
Wire block persistence: either make BlockChain.AddBlock persist via a DB handle or connect the orphaned BlockchainRepository so heights remain monotonic across restarts (currently resets to genesis).
fix(blockchain): persist appended blocks via InitBlockChain persister closure + stop doubling genesis on reload; removed orphaned sqlite BlockchainRepository. Commits 93ffe26, 3198371.

The DI composition root (internal/app/wire.go) had 0% test coverage — the exact place where cross-DB-file / separate-pool wiring bugs would surface, with no end-to-end check that the assembled app actually works.
test(app): end-to-end Wire round-trip (create/mint/transfer + ledger + audit history). Commit 5965464. app coverage 0%->78.9%.

app.Wire built a CompositeEventBus whose AsyncBus spawned an event loop goroutine and whose PluginBus was empty; neither was subscribed, and App exposed no Close — each Wire() call leaked one idle goroutine. Resolved: Wire now uses a plain SyncEventBus; App.EventBus is the EventBus interface.
refactor(app): drop idle async/plugin buses from Wire (SyncEventBus), App.EventBus -> EventBus interface. Commit e55e529.
Keep eventBus.Publish inside the token tx callback (publish-first), accepting that an in-tx failure can leave a recorded event for an op that rolled back.
nodes.rationale: Moving Publish to after the tx commits would, on event-DB failure, leave the balance mutation committed with NO event and the nonce consumed — a real transfer missing from history that the caller cannot retry (worse). Phantom events only occur on rare in-tx failure paths (concurrency rejects, invariant violations); publish-first also preserves the nonce-consumption anti-replay property. Cross-DB atomicity (tokens.db/events.db share a file but different pools) is a known architectural limit.
alternatives_rejected: Route event writes through the same tx/pool

nodes.summary: v1.4 milestone: lift cmd/aurora/cmd coverage from 21.9% to 80%+ by testing every cobra command (lottery create/history/verify/export/import/stats/reset/db-info/version, nft mint/transfer/burn/get/list/history, oracle source/fetch/data/latest/template, token create/mint/transfer/approve/burn/balance/allowance/history/info/tui, voting candidate/voter/session/vote/results, root Execute/config). CLI is the primary user-facing surface — flag-parsing, output, and wiring bugs live untested here.

go test ./cmd/aurora/cmd/ -cover reports 21.9% (2026-08-11). Only helpers (sameStringSet, getTemplates/getTemplate, min, getGoVersion, init fns) and 4 small regression tests covered; all cobra RunE bodies, newTokenService, getNFTRepo/nftService, getVotingRepo/getVotingService, b64Encode, truncateBase64, Execute/initConfig/setDefaultConfig at 0%.

nodes.summary: lottery verify disambiguated ID-vs-height via fmt.Sscanf(input, "%d", &height), which accepts a PARTIAL numeric prefix. A 16-hex lottery ID that begins with a decimal digit (e.g. 07551e0cac54a4cf) was misread as a block height and reported 'lottery not found' even though the draw existed. Found by CLI-coverage milestone testing.
nodes.evidence: cmd/aurora/cmd/lottery.go verifyCmd; caught by flaky full-package run of TestLotteryVerify_ByID (IDs random, ~10% start with a digit)

nodes.summary: 'aurora lottery reset' warns 'This will delete ALL lottery records!' but only runs DELETE FROM blocks WHERE height>0 — lottery_records rows survive, so history still lists them after reset. The warning overstates what the command does; the in-memory chain replay also repopulates blocks from genesis. Behavior pinned by test; not yet fixed.
nodes.evidence: cmd/aurora/cmd/lottery.go resetCmd; TestLotteryReset_WithYes documents actual behavior

nodes.summary: fix(cmd): lottery verify — exact-ID match first, height only when the whole input is a decimal integer (strconv.ParseInt), substring fallback last. Plus dedup test TestLotteryVerify_NumericPrefixID.

Migrations can never run: migrations/000001 starts with PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, but golang-migrate's sqlite3 driver wraps each migration in a transaction where WAL cannot be set → 'cannot change into wal mode from within a transaction'. RunMigrationsIfEnabled is only called from root.go PersistentPreRunE under migrate.autoRun (default false), and there is NO `aurora migrate` subcommand and cmd/api never migrates — so the voting/NFT/token schema from migrations is unreachable in the whole product. The migrate package's own tests use synthetic migrations, so this latent bug is untested.
nodes.evidence: go test cmd/aurora/cmd 'run migrations' reproduces the failure; migrate_test.go setupTestDB writes synthetic SQL without PRAGMA lines

nodes.summary: Even if migrations could apply, migrations/000001's blocks table (id AUTOINCREMENT + height UNIQUE, no timestamp column) contradicts what InitBlockChain actually creates/inserts (height PRIMARY KEY, has timestamp, no id). A migrated DB would break InitBlockChain's INSERT OR REPLACE. Since migrations have never successfully applied, no production DB has this schema — the discrepancy is latent but guarantees migrating a fresh DB corrupts the chain.
nodes.evidence: migrations/000001_init_schema.up.sql lines 9-17 vs internal/domain/blockchain/init.go CREATE TABLE blocks

nodes.summary: CLI voting subcommands (candidate add, voter register, session create) all fail with 'no such table: candidates/voters/voting_sessions' on a fresh temp DB because getVotingRepo builds over blockchain.InitDB() which only creates blocks; the voting tables exist only in the (un-appliable) migrations.

cmd/aurora/cmd statement coverage reached 86.3% (go test -cover, 2026-08-11) — above the 80% v1.4 milestone target, up from 21.9% baseline. All module command trees (lottery/nft/oracle/token/voting/root) now exercised with happy + error paths, green under -race.

fix(cmd): voting session create now accepts --start-time/--end-time (previously hardcoded 0/0 so session create could never succeed), and voting vote accepts --session (previously never set, so vote could never succeed). Added i18n keys. Found by v1.4 CLI coverage tests.

Voting CLI: session create hardcoded StartTime=0 EndTime=0 while usecase requires EndTime>StartTime → command could never succeed; vote never set SessionID → CastVoteUseCase always failed session lookup. Both made the voting workflow unusable from the CLI even when the schema existed.
chore(config): anchor **/aurora binary ignore to /aurora and /aurora-* so cmd/aurora/ source dir is not ignored; 4 pre-existing + new CLI test files are now tracked.

fix(migrations): remove PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL/PF-ON from 000001 (they can't run inside golang-migrate's tx wrapper; they are per-connection settings repos already apply) and reconcile the blocks table schema (height PRIMARY KEY + timestamp, no synthetic id) with InitBlockChain. Add regression tests applying the real checkout migrations (previously only synthetic migrations were tested).

UX gap: there is no `aurora migrate` subcommand and migrate.autoRun defaults to false, so a fresh install still has no voting/NFT/token tables unless the user sets migrate.autoRun=true in config. The migration files now apply (fix-migrations), but nothing in the CLI surface runs them by default. Consider adding a `migrate up/status` subcommand or flipping the default.

After the migration fix, the full voting CLI flow (candidate add → session create → voter register → vote) passes against the REAL checkout migrations with no schema bootstrapping. CLI voting tests switched from bootstrapVotingSchema workaround to runMigrations; real_migrations_test.go applies the actual migrations and asserts all 13 tables.

fix(cmd): lottery reset now deletes BOTH blocks and lottery_records (previously only blocks, so history still listed draws after reset, contradicting the 'delete ALL lottery records' warning). Tolerates 'no such table' on fresh DBs. Harden TestLotteryVerify_ByID_Startswith against all-numeric 8-char id prefixes (height-vs-ID ambiguity) with a deterministic numeric-prefix-is-height test.

Verified 2026-08-11: no `aurora migrate*` subcommand exists in cmd/aurora/cmd (no Use:/MigrateCmd matches); root.go PersistentPreRunE runs migrate.RunMigrationsIfEnabled only when migrate.autoRun is true, and setDefaultConfig sets migrate.autoRun=false (root.go:131) with migrate.path='./migrations'. v1.1-REQUIREMENTS marks MIG-03 'Migration CLI command' complete — a documented-but-absent feature. Fresh-install voting/NFT/token tables are unreachable from the CLI (all fail 'no such table').
nodes.detail: cmd/aurora/cmd/root.go:42-73 (PersistentPreRunE), root.go:127-139 (setDefaultConfig); internal/infra/migrate/migrate.go New/Up/Down/Status/Version/Close fully implemented and 81.5% covered

nodes.summary: Full-package `go test ./... -cover` 2026-08-11: internal/logger 55.2%, internal/i18n 65.2%, internal/infra/backup 73.8%, internal/ui/nft 66.7%, internal/ui/token 76.6% — the only packages below the 80% quality bar. cmd/aurora + cmd/api 0% are thin main() boots (documented out of scope); e2e is a test-only package (0% statements, suite itself green).
nodes.detail: measurement only; existing v1.4 milestone target 86.3% for cmd/aurora/cmd

nodes.summary: v1.5 = Fresh-Install Operations & Coverage Bar: add `aurora migrate up/down/status` CLI (restores the v1.1-documented MIG-03 surface that was never actually shipped) and lift every sub-80% package (logger/i18n/backup/ui-nft/ui-token) to ≥80%, the project's documented quality bar.
nodes.rationale: v1.4 proved exercising the real CLI surface exposes genuine product bugs. It surfaced that the migrator (internal/infra/migrate, 81.5% covered) is implemented and tested but unreachable: autoRun defaults false and no subcommand exists, so a fresh install cannot create the voting/NFT/token schema and those CLIs fail with 'no such table'. Closing that gap is the highest-value user-facing fix; the coverage sweep is the direct continuation of the 80% bar met everywhere else. Keeps accepted-debt NFT/voting transaction conversion deferred (no touchpoint trigger this milestone).
alternatives_rejected: Deep-dive NFT/voting real-transaction conversion (issue-nft-voting-no-transactions) — accepted debt, no trigger
Lift cmd/api + cmd/aurora main() from 0% — thin process boots, exit paths not testable in-process
Add a binary-level e2e harness for the migrate command — cobra CLI tests cover the command; service e2e suite exists

nodes.summary: Add `aurora migrate up [N] | down [N] | status` subcommand wired to the existing internal/infra/migrate.Migrator (New/Up/Down/Status/Version/Close). DB path resolution mirrors root (db.path → data.dir/aurora.db → ~/.aurora/data/aurora.db); migration path from migrate.path (default ./migrations). Cover happy + error paths with cobra CLI tests.
Lift internal/logger (55.2%), internal/i18n (65.2%), internal/infra/backup (73.8%) to ≥80% statement coverage with genuine tests, no weakening.
Lift internal/ui/nft (66.7%) and internal/ui/token (76.6%) to ≥80%, following the ui/lottery (91.7%) / ui/oracle (86.1%) TUI state-machine testing pattern.
